detail.longDescription: “I recently asked AI to help me look through the latest Windows binaries for undocumented features and functionality. Among the leads it turned up, one list immediately caught my attention: coding agents such as codex.exe, claude.exe, copilot.exe, and cursor.exe, alongside familiar developer tools such as python.exe, dotnet.exe, gcc.exe, and code.exe. Why would a Windows system DLL need a list of coding agents and developer tools? The names were in MissionControlAggregator.dll. I asked the agent to follow the references and dig into what the DLL actually does. That led from a handful of string comparisons to a running Windows component that records which coding agents and developer tools have been used, saves that information locally, and reports it to Windows Diagnostics. And unless you have opted out of the “optional” diagnostic data (which is enabled by default), the data is uploaded to Microsoft.” https:// xusheng.dev/posts/windows-codi ng-agent-telemetry/ # Microsoft # Windows # Privacy # Surveillance # AI # AIAgents # Telemetry # CodingAgents
